title: Deterministic Goldreich–Levin state sequence
statement: Let $n>0$, and let $a,b$ be positive integers with $2a\le b$, together with an integer Fourier bound $B\ge1$. For a Boolean function $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, define a sequence of states indexed by the nonnegative integers. The initial state has active family $\{\varnothing\}$ and empty trace; at stage $k+1$, if $k<n$ and the preceding active family exists with size at most the active cap determined by the input threshold, update the state by the Goldreich–Levin query step at coordinate $k$, using the estimate records computed from $f$; if that family exceeds the cap, make the active family absent and preserve the trace. In all other cases, retain the preceding state unchanged.
